data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A test constrains its subject rather than describes it when the subject's acceptance is conditional on the test's failure being impossible \u2014 the shown-to-fail-first installation turns the test into a sufficiency condition, so the subject is only what survives the test.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the test is not a necessary condition for acceptance, the sufficiency claim is too strong.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the mutation loss is due to an independent coverage gap, the constraint interpretation is not warranted.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the distribution is explained by registry size or module complexity, the sufficiency condition is confounded.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the same author's other modules lose 4/4 to 6/7 under the same ritual, the sufficiency condition is not stable.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The constraint relation is modal: the test sets a boundary that the subject cannot cross after installation. The 1/9 mutation lost in compile.py under shown-to-fail-first installation indicates that the boundary was set too narrowly \u2014 the guard covered declared data but not added behaviour, so the test constrained only a subset of the subject. The 3-of-26 distribution suggests the boundary is uneven across modules.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
